Resolves #4514

Decouples `Neo.component.Toast#closable_` (which renders the `.neo-toast-close` dismiss button) from `removeDelay` (which schedules automatic fade-out dismissal after mount whenever `removeDelay > 0`), and guards `Toast#destroy` against duplicate fade-out listeners when manual dismissal precedes timeout expiry.

Evidence: L1 (Playwright unit suite `test/playwright/unit/component/Toast.spec.mjs`) → L1 required (component config/lifecycle contract).

## AC Evidence
No structured ACs on #4514

| Scope Item | Verification |
|---|---|
| `closable: true` and `removeDelay > 0` renders close button and auto-dismisses after timeout | `test/playwright/unit/component/Toast.spec.mjs` (`closable: true and removeDelay > 0 renders close button and auto-dismisses after timeout (#4514)`) |
| `closable: true` with `removeDelay: 0` (or `null`) remains sticky | `test/playwright/unit/component/Toast.spec.mjs` (`closable: true with removeDelay: 0 remains sticky and does not auto-dismiss`) |
| Manual `destroy()` before `removeDelay` expires is idempotent and prevents duplicate fade-out | `test/playwright/unit/component/Toast.spec.mjs` (`manual destroy before removeDelay expires is idempotent and prevents duplicate fade-out`) |

## Deltas from ticket
- Wrapped `me.timeout(me.removeDelay)` in `me.trap(...)` inside `afterSetMounted` and added a fade-out guard in `destroy()` so manual dismissal before timeout expiry never double-registers `animationend` or leaks an unhandled `Neo.isDestroyed` rejection.
- Triggered `this.update()` in `afterSetClosable` when `closable` is mutated at runtime (`oldValue !== undefined`).
